formalization.project_name: Baire products with locally compact R1 factors

mathematical_sources.note: Directly consulted publisher PDF, Pacific Journal of Mathematics 48(1) (1973), 1–10, SHA256 538268e9276a75184874f44e4c7d79a64c5f1415caaaa5cd1f2da12de7651ceb. Printed pp.8–9, Section4.1 Projection Lemma, supplies the maximal disjoint open refinement/nested-fiber argument. Printed p.9 Section4.2 and its following corollary give a quasi-regular Baire first factor and, in particular, a locally compact Hausdorff second factor. This package specializes the completeness mechanism to compact neighborhoods, proves the arbitrary-first-factor/R1 formulation explicitly, and does not claim a literal match to all hypotheses or the full pseudocomplete theorem. The fixed nonempty open fiber region is explicit; empty products are separately included in the main theorem. No novelty, priority or first-formalization claim. Original Oxtoby1961 and White1975 full texts were not consulted.
mathematical_sources.title: Pseudo-completeness and the product of Baire spaces

mathematical_sources.note: Directly consulted author manuscript, 24Aug2017, PDF SHA256 e289b7691238657b2d686f21b2cb2bf0900a569e7db0bdd41045e501523ef47f. Printed pp.1–2 explain the productive-Baire research problem and completeness/game hypotheses that yield Baire products. This is research context, not a claim to formalize its stronger Choquet, Krom-space or hereditary-Baire theorems.
mathematical_sources.title: More on products of Baire spaces, arXiv:1702.06197v3

related_formalizations.note: Uses canonical product topology, IsGδ, Dense, BaireSpace, R1Space, LocallyCompactSpace, PositiveCompacts and compact closed-intersection infrastructure. The existing Mathlib single-space Baire theorem for locally compact R1 spaces and compact-neighborhood shrinking are credited, not presented as new. No equivalent product or dense-Gδ projection theorem was found in the bounded pinned-library audit. The substantive new bridge constructs maximal disjoint parameter refinements and coherent nested compact fibers. The sibling Kuratowski–Ulam package uses a countable pi-base instead; it is not imported and that assumption is absent here. MATERIAL-DEFINITIONS.md and verification/material-imported-definitions.json retain exact pinned definitions and dependency expansions for every material selected-surface predicate, including the R1 compact-closure and compact-to-weak-local-to-R1-local chain. Class-field equivalences are proved by constructor/projection, not mislabelled as definitional equality. Separate Challenge/Solution tests check the literal meanings and proved classical characterizations. Source/excerpt hashes authenticate bytes; independent review audits interpretation and coverage.
